proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\rho\in I\), the realized dataset, and a cell \(C=C_n(\rho)\) for which the displayed reference-cell probability is positive.  The Fisher completion assigns to every observed unit one known response under both candidate treatment labels.  Consequently, for every \((H'_{n,s},z'_{n1s})\in\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\), every summand in the candidate complement means and variances is known.  The exceptional cases are also imputable because the definition assigns the fixed value \(c_s-1\).  Thus \(X'_{n,s}\) and \(C'_n(\rho)\) are known for every candidate action.  The same completion determines every full-block midrank and hence \(R'_{1j}\); after a retained stratum receives a quota-respecting second-stage assignment it also determines \(R'_{2j}\) and \(T'_j\).  If \(C_s=0\), chronology supplies no second-stage coordinate.

By definition, \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\) imposes precisely the following conditions, each for every member of the fixed finite set \(S\): the holdout has size \(\lfloor\rho N_{n1s}\rfloor\); the first-stage assignment has quota \(m_{n1s}\); the recomputed complete signed label is \(C\); and, exactly when \(C_s=1\), the second-stage assignment has quota \(m_{n2s}\).  The preceding paragraph proves imputability on every history satisfying these conditions.

Conversely, a quota-respecting chronological history belongs to \(\prod_{s\in S}\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\) at stage one.  If its recomputed label is \(C\), it lies in the same-cell fiber; chronology then supplies a second-stage vector exactly for the coordinates with \(C_s=1\).  These are all the defining conditions of \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\).  Since \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}>0\), normalization on this finite support is defined.  There is no additional event in either direction.

For each \(t\in S\), let \(\mathcal H_{nt}\) be its holdout and stage-one history.  The holdout and stage-one design assumptions make \((\mathcal H_{nt})_{t\in S}\) mutually independent.  The variable \(X_{n,t}\) and its signed selection event are stratum-local measurable functions.  Conditional on the combined first-stage history, the second-stage assumption supplies independent stratum-local kernels.  Equivalently one may pre-generate those kernels and reveal only the recruited coordinates.  Thus, for \(j=(C,s)\in J\) and measurable \(B_0\), finite-product independence yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\in B_0,E_{n,C}(\rho)\}\\
&\quad=\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\in B_0,X_{n,s}>c_s\}
\prod_{t\in S\setminus\{s\}}p_{nt}^{C_t}(1-p_{nt})^{1-C_t}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking \(B_0\) to be the whole space gives the corresponding cell probability, and division cancels every factor with \(t\ne s\) whenever that probability is positive.

Under \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,\mathrm{base}}\), both the candidate mass and the completed selector map factor over the fixed finite set \(S\).  Hence its signed cell probability is \(\prod_{t\in S}(p'_{nt})^{C_t}(1-p'_{nt})^{1-C_t}\).  Restriction to \(C'_n=C\) divides by this product, and the subsequent second-stage law is an independent product over retained strata.  The assumed positivity of \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}\) justifies the division.  The independent Gaussian blocks give the same calculation.

For the active coordinate write
\[
X_s=a_j(\rho)h_s+Z,
\qquad
T_j=d_j(\theta_j)h_s+r_j(\rho,\theta_j)Z+v_j(\rho,\theta_j)E,
\]
where \(Z,E\) are independent standard normals.  Under the null, selection is \(Z>c_s\), so integrating over \(E\) gives the defining equation for \(q_{\alpha,j}\).  Under the local alternative, selection is \(Z>c_s-a_j(\rho)h_s\), and the same integration gives exactly \(\Pi_j\).  Thus no signed inequality belonging to another coordinate of the complete cell has been discarded.

Fix a block and suppress its indices.  From \(\max_i x_i^4\le\sum_i x_i^4\) and the fourth-moment condition,
\[
\max_i(B_i-\bar B)^2
\le\left\{\sum_i(B_i-\bar B)^4\right\}^{1/2}
\le\sqrt{M_4N}.
\]
The variance margin gives \(\sum_i(B_i-\bar B)^2=(N-1)S_B^2\ge(N-1)\epsilon\), proving the first claimed ratio bound.  Since \(0\le U_i^0\le1\), one has \(\max_i(U_i^0-\bar U^0)^2\le1\), while the same margin gives a denominator at least \((N-1)\epsilon\).  Positive shares imply \(N_{nks}\to\infty\) uniformly over the fixed finite set \(K\times S\).  Both displayed ratios therefore converge uniformly to zero, and every division is licensed by \(\epsilon>0\).

Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the defining covariance ratio gives \(\lvert\kappa_j\rvert\le1\).  Since \(\rho\in[\rho_0,1-\rho_0]\) and \(0\le\cos^2\theta_j\le1\),
\[
v_j(\rho,\theta_j)^2
=1-\kappa_j^2(1-\rho)\cos^2\theta_j
\ge1-(1-\rho)=\rho\ge\rho_0>0.
\]
This calculation concerns only the limiting Gaussian covariance and asserts no finite-sample covariance inequality.

Fix one admissible baseline array \(B=(B_n)_n\).  All uniformities below are over the displayed compact parameter sets for this array; there is no supremum over different arrays.

For a stage-one block write \(N=N_{n1s}\), \(m=m_{n1s}\), \(\delta=h_s/\sqrt n\), and let \(G\) be the random complement.  The hypergeometric mean and variance formulas, the bounds \(\rho_0\le\rho\le1-\rho_0\), and balanced quotas give, uniformly in \(\rho\),
\[
\frac{g^1}{N}\xrightarrow{\mathsf P}\frac{1-\rho}{2},
\qquad
\frac{g^0}{N}\xrightarrow{\mathsf P}\frac{1-\rho}{2}.
\]
For \(f_i\) equal to \(B_i-\bar B\), \((B_i-\bar B)^2\), or \((B_i-\bar B)(U_i^0-\bar U^0)\), the simple-random-sampling variance identity and Cauchy--Schwarz with the fourth-moment bound imply
\[
|G|^{-1}\sum_{i\in G}f_i-N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^Nf_i=o_{\mathsf P}(1)
\]
uniformly over the admissible complement sizes.  Conditioning on the treatment quota and applying the same identity within \(G\) gives the corresponding statement for either arm; the preceding count limit bounds the random denominators away from zero with probability tending to one.  Hence both arm variances converge to their finite-population limits, the exceptional totalization event vanishes, and direct studentization yields
\[
X_{n,s}=A_s\sqrt{1-\rho}\,h_s+X^0_{n,s}+o_{\mathsf P}(1),
\]
where \(X^0_{n,s}\) is the standardized complement contrast of the fixed baselines.

For ranks, let \(K_N(\delta)\) be the ordered-pair crossing count.  Complete-randomization inclusion probabilities give
\[
\mathsf E(\text{treated crossed-pair count})
=\frac{m(N-m)}{N(N-1)}K_N(\delta).
\]
Writing the variance as a double sum of ordered edges, pairs sharing a vertex contribute at most a constant times \(NK_N(\delta)\), whereas disjoint pairs have covariance of order \(N^{-1}\) and contribute at most a constant times \(K_N(\delta)^2/N\).  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\text{crossed-pair count})
\le C\{NK_N(\delta)+K_N(\delta)^2/N\}.
\]
The uniform pair-spacing condition gives \(K_N(\delta)=O(N^{3/2})\).  After division by the null rank-sum standard deviation, which is of order \(N^{3/2}\), the centered crossing term is \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\), while its expectation converges to the stated drift.  If \(d_i\) is the number of crossings incident to unit \(i\), then
\[
\frac1N\sum_i(d_i/N)^2\le\frac{2K_N(\delta)}{N^2}=O(N^{-1/2}),
\]
so the observed ranks and baseline ranks have the same limiting variance and covariance.  The pair-spacing premise also makes the squared empirical tie masses vanish, whence the normalized-midrank variance tends to \(1/12\).  Consequently
\[
R_{1j}=b_{1j}h_s+R^0_{1j}+o_{\mathsf P}(1),
\qquad
R_{2j}=b_{2j}h_s+R^0_{2j}+o_{\mathsf P}(1).
\]

Conditional on a nonexceptional holdout, every scalar projection of \((X^0_{n,s},R^0_{1j})\) obeys the maximum-influence condition proved in \(\mathrm{lem{:}derived\mbox{-}max\mbox{-}influence}\).  The cited finite-population vector central limit theorem applies.  A covariance calculation with \(W_i=2Z_i-1\), using \(\mathsf E(W_iW_l)=-1/(N-1)\) for \(i\ne l\), gives
\[
\operatorname{Corr}(X^0_{n,s},R^0_{1j})
\longrightarrow\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho};
\]
the complement indicator contributes one factor \(1-\rho\) to covariance and one square-root factor to the selector standard deviation.  Stage two is independent conditional on the history.  Since \(S\) and \(J\) are fixed and finite, the cited vector theorem applies to the concatenated fixed-dimensional vector.  It follows that
\[
(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\Longrightarrow
\mathcal N\!\left(
\begin{pmatrix}A_s\sqrt{1-\rho}h_s\\b_{1j}h_s\\b_{2j}h_s\end{pmatrix},
\begin{pmatrix}
1&\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}&0\\
\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}&1&0\\
0&0&1
\end{pmatrix}
\right).
\]
Uniformity follows by subsequences: a violating sequence of \((\rho,h,\theta)\) has a convergent subsequence, and the uniform share, moment, pair-spacing, and influence bounds give the same limit along it.  The residual-scale lemma excludes singular projected limits.

For the Fisher reference, the completed stage-one values are \(B_i+\delta Z_i\).  Their centered second and fourth moments differ from those of \(B\) by \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\), and their normalized ranks differ in empirical squared norm by \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\) by the crossing-degree bound.  Candidate treatment labels and holdouts are freshly randomized from their product law, so every candidate contrast is null-centered; candidate stage-two assignments are independent after the candidate cell is retained.  The same finite-population argument therefore makes the pre-cell reference vector converge, in the corresponding \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\)-probability and uniformly in \((\rho,h,\theta)\), to the same Gaussian vector with all drifts zero.

Rectangle convergence at the fixed thresholds transfers both joint numerators and cell probabilities.  The sampling margin bounds the true denominators below by \(\epsilon\), and the reference margin does so with probability tending to one.  The conditioning-ratio lemma and the finite-product factorization then yield the two asserted uniform conditional-cdf limits.  The inequality \(v_j^2\ge\rho_0\), finiteness of \(S,J\), compactness of the parameters, and Gaussian tail bounds place all null critical values in one compact interval and give a positive lower density bound on a slightly larger interval.  The quantile part of the ratio lemma therefore transfers the random reference quantiles uniformly.

Let \(a_n=d_n^{\mathrm{samp}}(B)\), and let \(Z_n(\rho,h)\) denote the reference distance.  The preceding steps show \(a_n\to0\) and, for every \(u>0\),
\[
\sup_{\rho\in I,h\in H}\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{Z_n(\rho,h)>u\}\to0.
\]
Choose \(N_m\uparrow\infty\) so that for \(n\ge N_m\), \(a_n\le1/m\) and the last supremum at \(u=1/m\) is at most \(1/m\).  Defining \(\eta_n(B)=1/m\) on \([N_m,N_{m+1})\), with finitely many initial terms enlarged, gives the common decreasing remainder.

Finally bracket the rejection event on the event that its random critical value is within \(\zeta\) of \(q_{\alpha,j}\).  The complement has probability tending to zero; on the bracketed event the sampling cdf is evaluated at \(q_{\alpha,j}\pm\zeta\).  Gaussian anti-concentration, followed by \(\zeta\downarrow0\), gives the rejection limit.  The factorization lemma identifies that limit with \(\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\).  This proves the stated field-level sampling and reference transfer with one array-dependent remainder.

Let \(\gamma_2\) be standard Gaussian measure on \(\mathbb R^2\) and define
\[
\mathcal T(c,z)=Q^{-1}\{Q(c)Q(z)\}.
\]
Minkowski interpolation of the orthants \([c,\infty)\times[z,\infty)\) interpolates their thresholds.  The cited Ehrhard--Borell inequality and \(Q^{-1}(u)=-\Phi^{-1}(u)\) therefore show that \(\mathcal T\) is jointly convex.  Moreover, for standard normal \(Z\),
\[
\Pr\{\mathcal T(c,Z)>y\}=\frac{Q(y)}{Q(c)},\qquad y>c,
\]
so \(\mathcal T(c,Z)\) has the law of a standard normal conditioned to exceed \(c\).

Put \(v=(1-r^2)^{1/2}>0\), \(W(c,z,e)=r\mathcal T(c,z)+ve\), and
\[
\mathcal A(c,q)=\{(z,e):W(c,z,e)\le q\}.
\]
For \(r\ge0\), convexity gives
\[
(1-t)\mathcal A(c_0,q_0)+t\mathcal A(c_1,q_1)
\subseteq\mathcal A((1-t)c_0+tc_1,(1-t)q_0+tq_1).
\]
Taking \(q_i=q_\beta(r,c_i)\), both left sets have Gaussian measure \(1-\beta\).  Ehrhard--Borell, the inclusion, and uniqueness of the quantile (supplied by the independent \(vE\) term) imply
\[
q_\beta(r,(1-t)c_0+tc_1)
\le(1-t)q_\beta(r,c_0)+tq_\beta(r,c_1).
\]

If \(r=0\), this quantile is constant; if \(c_0=c_1\), chord equality is tautological.  Conversely suppose \(r>0\), \(c_0\ne c_1\), and equality holds.  Equality must then hold in the Gaussian-set comparison.  By the cited equality classification, the two closed convex sets \(\mathcal A(c_i,q_i)\) are parallel half-spaces or equal up to null sets.  Their boundaries
\[
e=\{q_i-r\mathcal T(c_i,z)\}/v
\]
are not affine because \(\mathcal T(c,z)\to c\) as \(z\to-\infty\) and tends to infinity as \(z\to\infty\).  Equality up to null sets between closed convex sets with nonempty interiors is equality, so \(\mathcal T(c_0,z)-\mathcal T(c_1,z)\) would be constant.  Its limit at \(-\infty\) is \(c_0-c_1\).  Integration by parts gives the needed Mills bounds: \(Q(x)<x^{-1}\int_x^\infty t\phi(t)\,dt=\phi(x)/x\), while \(Q(x)=\phi(x)/x-\int_x^\infty\phi(t)t^{-2}\,dt>\phi(x)/x-Q(x)/x^2\).  Hence
\[
\frac{\phi(x)}{x+x^{-1}}<Q(x)<\frac{\phi(x)}x\qquad(x>0)
\]
make the ratio of the two tails tend to zero or infinity as \(z\to\infty\), whereas the defining identity makes it the finite constant \(Q(c_0)/Q(c_1)\).  Thus the constant is zero and \(c_0=c_1\), a contradiction.

Fix \(j=(C,s)\), \(\rho\), and \(\theta_j\), and abbreviate \(a=a_j(\rho)>0\), \(d=d_j(\theta_j)>0\), and \(r=r_j(\rho,\theta_j)\).  For \(u\in(\alpha,1)\), the selected-quantile definition gives
\[
\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\ge u
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
B_u(h_s):=dh_s+q_u(r,c_s-ah_s)-q_\alpha(r,c_s)\ge0.
\]
The selected-quantile theorem makes \(B_u\) continuous and convex.  Since \(u>\alpha\), \(B_u(0)<0\).  As \(h_s\to\infty\), the selected threshold tends to \(-\infty\), its selected quantile tends to the ordinary Gaussian quantile, and \(dh_s\to\infty\); hence \(B_u(h_s)\to\infty\).  A convex function negative at zero has at most one positive transition from negative to nonnegative: at a zero \(x>0\), every right secant slope is at least \(\{B_u(x)-B_u(0)\}/x>0\).  Thus its nonnegative set on \((0,\infty)\) is an upper interval.

Compactness of \(H\) attains \(\ell_s=\min_{h\in H}h_s>0\), and every other admissible coordinate is at least \(\ell_s\).  The upper-interval property proves the stated equivalence.  The feasible pure-stage-two weight \(\theta_j=\pi/2\) has \(r=0\) and power
\[
Q\{\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha)-b_{2j}h_s\}>\alpha.
\]
Therefore all optimized cell values and the global optimized value exceed \(\alpha\).  Equality of all superlevel predicates above \(\alpha\) implies equality of both optimized values and complete argmax sets.  This argument is coordinatewise and uses only finiteness of \(J\), not a two-coordinate property.

Fix an active pair and suppress its index.  Put \(t=\sqrt{1-\rho}\), \(a=At\), \(\gamma=\kappa t\), \(d=b_1\cos\theta+b_2\sin\theta\), \(r=\gamma\cos\theta\), and \(v=\sqrt{1-r^2}\).  For \(h=\ell_s>0\), set
\[
L=c-ah,\quad K=q_\alpha(r,c)-dh,\quad
u_0=\frac{c-rq_\alpha(r,c)}v,\quad
u_h=\frac{L-rK}v,
\quad D_h=\frac{\phi(K)Q(u_h)}{Q(L)}>0.
\]
Differentiation of the Gaussian tail integral and its null critical equation gives
\[
q_r=\frac{\mu(u_0)}v,\qquad P_d=hD_h,qquad
P_r=\frac{D_h}{v}\{\mu(u_h)-\mu(u_0)\},
\]
where \(\mu(x)=\phi(x)/Q(x)\).  Every division is valid because \(v^2\ge\rho_0\) and Gaussian tails are positive.  The identity \(\mu'(x)=\mu(x)\{\mu(x)-x\}\) gives \(\mu'(x)>0\), because \(\mu(x)=\mathsf E(Z\mid Z>x)>x\).  Integration by parts also gives \(\operatorname{Var}(Z\mid Z>x)=1-\mu'(x)>0\), and hence \(\mu'(x)<1\).  Therefore the secant
\[
\bar s=\frac{\mu(u_0)-\mu(u_h)}{u_0-u_h}
\]
(with \(\mu'(u_0)\) at equality) lies in \((0,1)\), while \(u_0-u_h=h(a-rd)/v\).

With \(d'=b_2\cos\theta-b_1\sin\theta\) and \(r'=-\gamma\sin\theta\), the chain rule yields
\[
\frac{P_\theta}{hD_h}
=d'+\frac{\gamma\sin\theta\,(a-rd)\bar s}{v^2}.
\]
Using \(\cos\theta\,d=b_1+\sin\theta\,d'\) and \(\Delta=A-\kappa b_1\), this becomes
\[
\frac{P_\theta}{hD_h}
=\mathcal Ld'+\frac{\kappa t^2\sin\theta\,\Delta\bar s}{v^2},
\qquad
\mathcal L=1-\frac{\gamma^2\sin^2\theta\,\bar s}{v^2}>0,
\]
because \(v^2-\gamma^2\sin^2\theta\bar s\ge1-\gamma^2\ge\rho>0\).  Now \(d'\) is positive below \(\theta_0=\arctan(b_2/b_1)\), zero there, and negative above.  If \(\Delta>0\), the derivative is positive throughout \([0,\theta_0]\); if \(\Delta<0\), it is negative throughout \([\theta_0,\pi/2]\), while \(P_\theta(0)=hb_2D_h>0\); and if \(\Delta=0\), its sign is exactly that of \(d'\).  Compactness supplies maximizers and proves all three claimed strata.  The least-coordinate theorem transfers the result to the original compact alternative set.

Fix a jointly realizable active stage-one block, center its empirical baseline law, and let its limiting variance and pair slope be \(\sigma^2>0\) and \(\lambda>0\).  Convolve the empirical law with the uniform density on an interval of width \(\delta_N=u_\star/\sqrt N\), where \([0,u_\star]\) is inside the pair-spacing window.  For the resulting density \(f_N\), the ordered-pair convention gives the exact overlap identity
\[
\|f_N\|_2^2
=\frac{2}{N^2\delta_N^2}\int_0^{\delta_N}K_N(u)\,du
=\frac{2}{u_\star^2}\int_0^{u_\star}N^{-3/2}K_N(x/\sqrt N)\,dx
\longrightarrow\lambda.
\]
Its variance is \(\sigma_N^2+\delta_N^2/12\), which tends to \(\sigma^2\) by the variance and share premises.

For any centered density \(f\) of variance \(\sigma_f^2>0\), take \(a=\sqrt5\sigma_f\) and \(g(x)=3(1-x^2/a^2)_+/(4a)\).  Since \((1-x^2/a^2)_+\ge1-x^2/a^2\),
\[
\int fg\ge\frac{3}{5a},
\qquad
\int g^2=\frac{3}{5a}.
\]
The inequality \(\int(f-g)^2\ge0\) gives \(\|f\|_2^2\sigma_f\ge3/(5\sqrt5)\).  Applying it to \(f_N\) gives \(\lambda\sigma\ge3/(5\sqrt5)\).

Pair spacing removes asymptotic atoms, so the normalized midrank variance tends to \(1/12\).  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(\operatorname{Cov}(B,U^0)\le\sigma/\sqrt{12}\).  Joint realizability and the definitions imply
\[
A=\frac{\sqrt{r_1}}{2\sigma},\qquad
b_1=\sqrt3\lambda\sqrt{r_1},\qquad
\kappa=\frac{\sqrt{12}\operatorname{Cov}(B,U^0)}\sigma.
\]
Consequently
\[
\frac{A\kappa}{b_1}
=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(B,U^0)}{\sigma^2\lambda}
\le\frac{1}{\sqrt{12}\sigma\lambda}
\le\frac{5\sqrt{15}}{18}.
\]
All denominators are positive by the primitive variance and pair-spacing conditions, and the argument is cellwise, hence uniform over finite \(J\).

Fix \(j\) with \(\Delta_j\ge0\) and write \(P(\rho,\theta)=\Pi_j(\rho,\theta,\ell_s)\).  In the notation of the weight-side proof, differentiation gives, for \(r>0\),
\[
P_a=h\mu(L)\left[Q\!\left(\frac{q-dh-rL}{v}\right)-P\right]<0,
\qquad
\operatorname{sign}(P_r)=\operatorname{sign}(rd-a).
\]
The strict inequality holds because conditional rejection probability increases strictly with the selected Gaussian coordinate, so its boundary value is below its selected-tail average.  Every individually optimal angle obeys \(\theta\ge\theta_0\), and on this interval \(\cos\theta\,d\le b_1\).  Hence
\[
a-rd=t\{A-\kappa\cos\theta\,d\}\ge t\Delta\ge0,
\]
so \(P_r\le0\).  Since \(a_\rho=-A/(2t)\) and \(r_\rho=-\kappa\cos\theta/(2t)\),
\[
P_\rho=-\frac{AP_a+\kappa\cos\theta P_r}{2t}>0
\]
at every optimal non-pure angle.  At \(\theta=\pi/2\), power is the constant \(p_2=Q\{\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha)-b_2\ell_s\}\).

At \(\rho=1-\rho_0\), the inward angular derivative from \(\pi/2\) is
\[
\phi\{\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha)-b_2h\}
\left[b_1h-\kappa t\{\mu(c)-\mu(c-Ath)\}\right].
\]
Because \(0<\mu'<1\), its bracket exceeds \(h(b_1-\kappa At^2)\).  The realizability bound and \(t^2=\rho_0<1/2\) yield
\[
\frac{\kappa At^2}{b_1}
\le\rho_0\frac{5\sqrt{15}}{18}<1,
\]
so the pure-stage-two value is strictly improvable at the endpoint.

Thus \(M_j(\rho)\) is strictly smaller at every \(\rho<1-\rho_0\): if its optimizer is pure stage two, its value is \(p_2\), below the endpoint value; otherwise its fixed-angle power strictly increases toward the endpoint.  Choose a cell binding in the finite minimum at the endpoint.  Its strict inequality implies
\[
F(\rho)<F(1-\rho_0)\qquad(\rho<1-\rho_0),
\]
proving uniqueness of the holdout fraction.  The weight-side theorem gives the binding-cell angle location and equality stratum, while the definition of \(\mathcal S^\star\) gives the stated superlevel sets for slack cells.

Before scaling, the stage-one density is \(16/5\) on \([-1/10,1/10]\) and \(1/5\) on the remainder of \([-1,1]\).  Direct integration gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(B)=\frac{203}{1500},\qquad
\int f^2=\frac{53}{25},\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}\{B,F(B)\}=\frac14\mathsf E|B-B'|=\frac{1393}{15000}.
\]
Scaling by \(L=53\sqrt3/80\) multiplies variance by \(L^2\), divides the pair slope by \(L\), and multiplies the covariance by \(L\).  The stage-two uniform law has variance \(625/1849\) and pair slope \(43/(50\sqrt3)\).  With share \(1/4\), substitution gives
\[
A=\frac{200\sqrt5}{53\sqrt{203}},\qquad
b_1=\frac85,\qquad b_2=\frac{43}{100},\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1393\sqrt5}{250\sqrt{203}}.
\]
Squaring positive quantities and comparing integers verifies the displayed outward rational-decimal enclosures and \(\Delta=A-\kappa b_1<0\).

Both supports are bounded by \(1.15\), so centered empirical fourth moments are eventually below \(2\).  Their variances and normalized-rank variances converge to constants exceeding \(1/100\), and all four block shares converge to \(1/4\).  Deterministic quantile Riemann sums for each bounded piecewise-constant density give
\[
N^{-3/2}K_N(u/\sqrt N)\longrightarrow u\int f^2
\]
uniformly on fixed compact \(u\)-windows.  The displayed singleton primitive vector is compact and jointly generated by this array.  The design assumptions and no interference hold by construction.

The split-assignment finite-population central limit theorem and studentizer consistency give, uniformly in \(\rho\),
\[
\Pr\{X_{n,s}>-113/100\}
\longrightarrow Q\{-113/100-A\sqrt{1-\rho}\,h_s\}
\ge Q(-113/100).
\]
Independence between the two witness strata gives the squared lower bound.  Under the Fisher completion, local shifts are \(O(n^{-1/2})\), do not change empirical second moments, and newly randomized candidate contrasts are null-centered.  The same conditional central limit theorem makes each candidate selection probability converge in sampling probability to \(Q(-113/100)\), uniformly in \((\rho,h)\); their product converges to its square.  Outward-rounded Gaussian evaluation gives
\[
Q(-113/100)^2\in[0.75822626517532,0.75822626517534]>1/100.
\]
Thus the two-stratum witness satisfies every member condition and both margins within the general finite-stratum theory.

The witness has exactly two active cells and identical primitives, so equal angles give equal cell powers.  The weight-side theorem restricts every endpoint maximizer to \(0<\theta<\theta_0\), because both discrepancies are negative.

The numerical inequalities are interval certificates using \(100\)-bit Arb balls.  At each queried design, the monotone null-tail equation was bracketed on opposite signs to width \(2\cdot10^{-7}\).  The power integral was evaluated outwardly on \([c-ah,12]\), and the omitted tail is below \(Q(12)<10^{-31}\).  At the rational interior point this yields
\[
\Pi_j(5034/10000,25363/100000,33/20)
\in[0.8642862126664672633,0.8642862583791498921].
\]
On \(0\le\theta\le\theta_0\), direct differentiation gives the certified Lipschitz bound
\[
|\partial_\theta\Pi_j|
\le\frac{h}{\sqrt{2\pi}Q(c-ah)}
\left[b_2+
\frac{\gamma\sin\theta_0\{a+\gamma\sqrt{b_1^2+b_2^2}\}}
{1-\gamma^2}\right]=:L_\theta,
\]
whose denominators are positive because \(\gamma^2\le1-\rho_0<1\).  A \(129\)-point uniform mesh, enlarged by \(L_\theta\theta_0/256\), certifies
\[
\sup_{\theta\in[0,\pi/2]}\Pi_j(0.02,\theta,33/20)
\le0.8630457385441023483,
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\theta\in[0,\pi/2]}\Pi_j(0.98,\theta,33/20)
\le0.8624116251942651582.
\]
The weight-side restriction covers the unmeshed complement.  Both endpoint bounds are below the certified interior lower bound.  The transfer theorem identifies these as limiting rejection powers with a shifted sampling law and a separate zero-drift reference critical law.  Compactness gives an optimizer; neither endpoint can be one, so every maximizing holdout fraction is interior.

Fix a primitive stratum and \(j=(C,s)\in J\).  Set \(p_j(\rho,\vartheta)=\Pi_j(\rho,\vartheta,\ell_s)\) on \(D_j=I\times[0,\pi/2]\).  The residual bound keeps \(r_j\) in a compact subset of \((-1,1)\).  The null selected-tail map
\[
H_s(q,r)=Q(c_s)^{-1}\int_{c_s}^{\infty}
\phi(z)Q\!\left(\frac{q-rz}{\sqrt{1-r^2}}\right)\,dz
\]
is real analytic, by differentiation under a common Gaussian envelope, and
\[
\partial_qH_s(q,r)=-\frac{1}{Q(c_s)\sqrt{1-r^2}}
\int_{c_s}^{\infty}\phi(z)
\phi\!\left(\frac{q-rz}{\sqrt{1-r^2}}\right)\,dz<0.
\]
The analytic implicit-function theorem makes \(q_{\alpha,j}\), and hence \(p_j\), analytic on a neighborhood of \(D_j\).

Let \(Z_j=\{\partial_\vartheta p_j=0\}\cap D_j\).  It has no two-dimensional open component: otherwise analytic continuation would make \(p_j(\rho,\cdot)\) constant, contradicting the weight-side theorem in each of the positive, negative, and zero discrepancy strata.  The cited semianalytic stratification theorem therefore decomposes \(Z_j\), compatibly with projection and the boundary, into finitely many point and arc strata.  After finitely many cuts, each rank-one projected arc is an analytic graph \(\vartheta=\vartheta_{j\ell}(\rho)\); its ramified endpoints have the retained Weierstrass--Puiseux continuation.  Vertical arcs project to retained points, and angular endpoints are included.

Continuity gives an angular maximizer, and Fermat's rule puts every interior maximizer in \(Z_j\).  Hence on every projected stratum
\[
M_j(\rho)=\max_{\ell\in L_j}g_{j\ell}(\rho),
\qquad
g_{j\ell}(\rho)=p_j(\rho,\vartheta_{j\ell}(\rho)),
\]
with finitely many analytic or Puiseux-continuable branches.  Because \(J\) is fixed and finite, refining by every branch crossing, multiple root, endpoint, value tie, and identical-branch predicate remains a finite semianalytic refinement.  On each remaining interval the order is fixed, so
\[
F(\rho)=\min_{j\in J}M_j(\rho)
\]
equals a retained branch, with all ties recorded.

An interior maximizer on a nonconstant active branch is a stationary root.  A constant maximizing branch contributes its entire flat interval; all other maximizers are interval endpoints, projected endpoints, or retained intersections and ties.  Conversely, every listed candidate attaining \(V^\star\) is a maximizer by definition.  This proves necessity and sufficiency of the holdout list.

For fixed \(\rho\), separate cell-specific angles give
\[
\max_{\theta\in[0,\pi/2]^J}\min_{j\in J}p_j(\rho,\theta_j)
=\min_{j\in J}M_j(\rho)=F(\rho).
\]
The least-coordinate theorem makes this the original alternative-set problem.  Therefore, at a maximizing holdout, the complete weight correspondence is exactly
\[
\prod_{j=(C,s)\in J}
\{\theta_j\in[0,\pi/2]:
\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s)\ge V^\star\}.
\]
This retains all slack-cell continua.  No argument used \(|S|=2\) or a common sign of \(\Delta\); finiteness of \(S\) and \(J\) is the only product and stratification requirement.  The endpoint theorem and the two-stratum negative witness supply the stated special regimes.

On the compact domain \(D=I\times[0,\pi/2]^J\), define
\[
\Psi(\rho,\theta)=\min_{j=(C,s)\in J}\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s).
\]
For rational or algebraic inputs, Taylor expansion with rational remainder bounds encloses \(\phi\), while integration by parts gives
\[
Q(M)\le\frac{\phi(M)}M\qquad(M>0).
\]
Truncation at a computably increasing rational \(M\), bounded-interval quadrature, and outward rounding thus enclose every Gaussian integral and derivative to arbitrary prescribed accuracy.  Finiteness of \(S,J\) permits common bounds.

Choose a certified rational \(\underline q_c<\min_{s\in S}Q(c_s)\) and \(M_q\) so that \(Q(M_q)<\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\underline q_c\).  Since \(rZ+\sqrt{1-r^2}E\) is standard normal, conditioning on \(Z>c_s\) shows every null critical value lies in \([-M_q,M_q]\).  The residual bound and restriction of the derivative integral to \([c_s,c_s+1]\) give a computable common positive lower bound on \(|\partial_qH_s|\).  Bisection therefore terminates uniformly.  The alternative selection denominators also have a positive common bound on the compact domain, so differentiation gives an effective finite Lipschitz constant \(L\) for \(\Psi\), using
\[
|\min_j u_j-\min_j v_j|\le\max_j|u_j-v_j|.
\]

Subdivide \(D\) into finitely many rational boxes and evaluate each center accurately enough that
\[
L_B\le\Psi(x)\le U_B\quad(x\in B),
\qquad U_B-L_B\le\delta\le\varepsilon.
\]
Let \(L^\star=\max_BL_B\) and \(U^\star=\max_BU_B\).  A maximizing box and the boxwise widths imply
\[
L^\star\le V^\star\le U^\star\le L^\star+\delta.
\]
Boxes with \(U_B\ge L^\star\) contain every optimizer and consist only of points with power at least \(V^\star-2\varepsilon\).  Boxes with \(L_B\ge U^\star-\varepsilon\) form a nonempty inner union contained in the \(\varepsilon\)-superlevel set.  All comparisons are rational interval comparisons.

If the optional separation data are supplied, interval root-uniqueness tests isolate each claimed branch root, complement bounds exclude all others, strict interval comparisons eliminate competing values, and a positive objective gap excludes the complement.  Applying the same procedure to every factor in the finite product of weight superlevel sets excludes slack alternatives.  Only this certificate licenses a singleton assertion; absent it, the algorithm returns the value interval and set boxes just proved.

Apply the conditioning-ratio lemma with \(\delta=\eta_n(B)\) and \(m=m_n\).  It gives conditional-cdf error at most
\[
\frac{2\eta_n(B)}{m_n-\eta_n(B)},
\]
which vanishes under \(\eta_n(B)=o(m_n)\).  If the limiting density near the critical quantile is bounded below by \(g_n>0\), the quantile error is at most \(2\eta_n(B)/\{g_n(m_n-\eta_n(B))\}\); threshold bracketing then transfers power.

Necessity cannot be expressed through the declared remainder.  If \(\eta_n(B)\) is valid, any decreasing \(\widetilde\eta_n(B)\ge\eta_n(B)\) tending to zero is also valid, although its ratio to \(m_n\) can differ.  Absolute numerator and denominator errors may also cancel in their ratio.  Finally, the two frozen margin assumptions bound every represented cell probability below by the fixed \(\epsilon>0\), so \(m_n\downarrow0\) does not occur within \(\mathcal M\).  A sharp frontier would require an enlarged class, a canonical minimal modulus, and moving-boundary conditions; none is supplied by the frozen primitives.

Put \(p_n=P_n(E_n)\), \(p=P(E)\), \(a_n(x)=P_n(A_n(x))\), and \(a(x)=P(A(x))\).  Then \(p_n\ge m-\delta>0\) and \(0\le a(x)\le p\).  Therefore
\[
\left|\frac{a_n(x)}{p_n}-\frac{a(x)}p\right|
\le\frac{|a_n(x)-a(x)|}{p_n}
+\frac{a(x)|p_n-p|}{p_np}
\le\frac{2\delta}{m-\delta}.
\]
Taking the supremum proves the cdf bound.  If \(q\) is the limiting \(p\)-quantile, the density condition gives \(F(q-t)\le p-gt\) and \(F(q+t)\ge p+gt\) for \(0<t<a\).  Whenever \(t>e/g\), uniform cdf error yields \(F_n(q-t)<p<F_n(q+t)\), so the generalized quantile satisfies \(q-t<q_n\le q+t\).  Letting \(t\downarrow e/g\) proves the quantile bound.

added_lemmas.statement: A finite family of real-analytic functions admits, locally, Weierstrass polynomial preparation and a compatible semianalytic stratification. A relatively compact semianalytic set consequently has finitely many connected components and a finite compatible stratification into connected real-analytic manifolds. Projections of relatively compact semianalytic sets are subanalytic, and the number of connected components of the fibers of a relatively compact subanalytic map is locally bounded. In dimension one, every punctured local semianalytic branch admits a real-analytic arc parametrization, with Puiseux preparation available as a proof mechanism. At a simple zero, the corresponding branch is an analytic graph by the analytic implicit-function theorem.

added_lemmas.statement: Consider a sequence of finite populations of fixed-dimensional vectors assigned by complete randomization to a fixed number of groups whose limiting proportions are positive. If every scalar projection satisfies the finite-population maximum-influence condition and the correlation matrices converge, then the coordinatewise variance-standardized vector of group-contrast estimators converges in distribution to the centered Gaussian vector having the limiting correlation matrix.

added_lemmas.statement:
For closed convex sets \(A_0,A_1\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(0<t<1\), Gaussian measure satisfies the Ehrhard--Borell inequality
\[
\Phi^{-1}\!\bigl(\gamma_d((1-t)A_0+tA_1)\bigr)\ge(1-t)\Phi^{-1}(\gamma_d(A_0))+t\Phi^{-1}(\gamma_d(A_1)).
\]
When both measures lie strictly between zero and one, equality for weights summing to one occurs only when the sets are parallel half-spaces or when \(A_0=A_1\), apart from Gaussian-null modifications.

added_lemmas.statement: In the adaptive-experiment framework of Freidling, Zhao, and Gao, Proposition 1 states that assumptions A1--A3 and selective validity under the corresponding conditional reference law imply superuniform selective \(p\)-values and selective type-I error control.  This validity implication does not require the statistic, selector, or action law to be imputable.

added_lemmas.statement: In the adaptive-experiment framework of Freidling, Zhao, and Gao, Proposition 2 states that A2--A3 give the conditional-law representation obtained by independent candidate-action resampling restricted to the same selector, while A1 together with imputability of the test statistic, selector, and action mass with respect to \(\mathcal G\) makes that reference distribution computable.

added_lemmas.statement: Under no interference and the random-holdout, stage-one, and stage-two design assumptions, the construction in \(\mathrm{def{:}fzg\mbox{-}augmented\mbox{-}action\mbox{-}map}\) is a specialization of the Freidling--Zhao--Gao adaptive-experiment representation.  Its product action mass verifies A1, exogenous randomization verifies A2, and dependence of second-stage recruitment and assignment on the first action only through \(C\) verifies A3.  Independent candidate-action resampling restricted to the same \(C\) gives their Definition 1 equations (5)--(7).  Under \(h=0\), duplicated outcomes make the statistic, selector, and action mass imputable with respect to constant \(\mathcal G\); their Proposition 2 then gives exactly \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\), while their Proposition 1 separately gives exact selective validity.  This is a specialization, not a class equivalence, and their broader multistage result supplies neither the selected Gaussian transfer nor the holdout-power optimizer.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For every \(s\), the pair \((D_{ns},Z_{n1s})\) has the product of a uniform fixed-size holdout law and a uniform fixed-quota treatment law.  Independence across the fixed finite set \(S\) gives exactly the displayed \(q_1\), which is known, positive on its support, and normalized; this is A1.  Both coordinates are drawn independently of the fixed potential-outcome schedule, so the required exogeneity is A2.  After the first action, \(X\) is computed and summarized by \(C\).  The recruited population is exactly \(\mathcal R_2(C)\), and the conditional assignment mass is \(q_2(\cdot\mid C)\); no other first-action feature enters that kernel.  This is A3.

An independent candidate draw from \(q_1\) is precisely a draw from \(\prod_s\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\).  Recomputing its selector and imposing \(C'=C\) restricts and normalizes this product mass; conditionally on the retained value, an independent candidate draw from \(q_2(\cdot\mid C)\) supplies exactly the stage-two product mass.  These are the resampling, same-selector restriction, and conditional product identities in equations (5)--(7) of their Definition 1.  The explicit-support lemma shows that the resulting support is exactly \(\Omega_{n,C}\), with no hidden fiber.

At \(h=0\), \(\widetilde Y(d,z)=B\) for every augmented label.  Hence \(T\), the recomputed selector \(\mathcal S_1=C\), and the already known masses \(q_1,q_2\) are imputable from constant \(\mathcal G\).  The cited Proposition 2 therefore identifies the computable law with \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\).  The cited Proposition 1 separately transfers superuniform validity; it does not use this imputability as a validity premise.  Nothing in either cited proposition asserts a Gaussian local-power limit or optimizes \(\rho\) or \(\theta\), establishing the stated boundary of the specialization.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(J\) is any fixed finite nonempty active set and \(\Delta_j=0\) for every \(j=(C,s)\in J\).  Then every cell has the unique individually optimal weight \(\theta_{0j}=\arctan(b_{2j}/b_{1j})\), and the unique maximizing holdout fraction is \(1-\rho_0\).  The complete optimal-design correspondence is
\[
\mathcal S^\star=
\{1-\rho_0\}\times
\prod_{j=(C,s)\in J}
\left\{\theta_j\in[0,\pi/2]:
\Pi_j(1-\rho_0,\theta_j,\ell_s)\ge V^\star\right\}.
\]
It is a singleton exactly when every displayed cellwise superlevel set is a singleton; in particular this holds when every cell binds at its individual envelope.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For each \(j\in J\), the zero-discrepancy clause of the weight-side theorem makes \(\theta_{0j}\) its unique individual maximizer for every holdout.  Since all discrepancies are nonnegative, the global-endpoint theorem makes \(1-\rho_0\) the unique maximizing holdout fraction.  At that holdout, the separate cell-specific coordinates imply
\[
\min_j\Pi_j(1-\rho_0,\theta_j,\ell_s)=V^\star
\]
if and only if every cell power is at least \(V^\star\); this is exactly the displayed Cartesian product.  A finite Cartesian product is a singleton exactly when each factor is.  If every cell binds, its factor is the set on which power reaches its individual maximum, which is \(\{\theta_{0j}\}\) by uniqueness.  No equality of primitives across cells is required.

prose_updates.tldr: For an arbitrary fixed finite nonempty stratum set \(S\), a common holdout fraction \(\rho\) indexes a chronological two-stage enrichment randomization and its same-design Fisher sharp-null reference. Stage-one randomized action is the pair of holdout and treatment vectors; this gives a formal specialization of Freidling--Zhao--Gao's augmented-action representation, with their Proposition 1 supplying validity independently of imputability and Proposition 2 supplying computability at the sharp null. A per-array common remainder transfers the shifted sampling cdf and the zero-drift data-dependent reference cdf on every complete signed cell. Finite-product factorization reduces each active cell to a scalar selected Gaussian power. Ehrhard--Borell convexity reduces arbitrary compact positive alternatives to their least coordinate, the sign of \(\Delta_j=A_s-\kappa_jb_{1j}\) fixes the side of the proportional stage weight, all nonnegative discrepancies force the largest holdout, and an explicit two-stratum mixture certifies an interior negative-discrepancy regime. Mixed signs have a complete equality-aware analytic branch characterization, while interval computation returns certified value and optimizer-set boxes and asserts uniqueness only with separation.

project_justification.gap: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao provide a broader adaptive-experiment validity and conditional-reference framework, but do not derive a finite-population selected Gaussian power limit or optimize a common holdout and cell-specific stage weights. Existing finite-population central limit theorems are unconditional, and Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu study nonnested normal model-based policies with a different expected-sample-size and familywise-error objective. None supplies the present field-level sampling/reference transfer and maximin conditional-power frontier over arbitrary fixed finite strata.
project_justification.niche: The missing design object is a fixed-finite-stratum, design-based maximin problem in which one scalar holdout changes both selection and retained first-stage information, while each active complete-cell coordinate has its own nonnegative unit-norm stage weight. The optimizer can be an endpoint, an interior point, or a set-valued mixed-sign correspondence.
project_justification.fill: The project embeds the stage-one action as \(\widetilde Z_{n1si}=(D_{nsi},Z_{n1si})\), with \(D_{nsi}=\mathbf 1\{i\in H_{n,s}\}\), duplicates potential outcomes across the holdout label, and verifies the FZG A1--A3 and same-selector resampling equations. At the sharp null, Proposition 2 computes the explicit chronological reference and Proposition 1 separately transfers exact validity. The new contribution then derives, for arbitrary fixed finite \(S\), a common per-array split-conditional Gaussian and reference transfer, scalar complete-cell power integrals, least-coordinate reduction, the \(\Delta\)-indexed weight theorem, a unique largest-holdout region, a certified two-stratum interior witness, full mixed-sign branch geometry, and tolerance-certified optimizer sets.

sampling_model.design: For each \(\rho\in I\), independently across every \(s\in S\), draw a simple-random fixed-size holdout and a balanced complete-randomization stage-one assignment. Compute the full signed cell \(C\in\{0,1\}^S\), recruit exactly its positive coordinates, and then independently completely randomize stage two only in recruited strata. The Fisher reference rerandomizes the joint augmented first action, recomputes the entire selector, restricts to the same \(C\), and then draws the appropriate stage-two product kernel.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite-population triangular array over two stages and an arbitrary fixed finite nonempty set of strata; assignment and holdout randomization are the only sources of randomness. The explicit array \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\) is a two-stratum subcase used only as the negative-discrepancy witness.
sampling_model.treatment: Balanced binary treatment is completely randomized in every stage-one stratum and, after recruitment, in every selected stage-two stratum under its history-conditional kernel. Holdout status augments the first randomized action but does not alter potential outcomes.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment quotas have positive limiting shares, represented complete signed cells have the fixed positive sampling and reference margins, and the limiting conditional residual variance is at least \(\rho_0\). All products and minima range over fixed finite \(S\) and \(J\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Random complement counts, the complement Neyman studentizer, normalized-midrank studentizers, pair-spacing slopes, and mean--rank correlations are controlled jointly in the finite-population transfer. Maximum influence is derived from the fourth-moment, variance-margin, and share primitives; no Gaussian limit is assumed.

prose_updates.related_work: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao's Definition 1 and Propositions 1--2 provide the broader adaptive-experiment representation specialized here. The exact map uses stage-one population \(\mathcal R_1\), augmented action \(D,Z_1\), selector \(\mathcal S_1=C\), selected population \(\mathcal R_2(C)\), and a constant sharp-null schedule \(\mathcal G\). Their Proposition 1 yields validity without imputability; A2--A3 in Proposition 2 yield the conditional-law representation, and A1 plus imputability yield computability. This is a specialization, not class equivalence, and their broader \(K\)-stage class supplies no selected Gaussian power frontier. Li and Ding supply the finite-population vector central limit theorem used after the present influence bounds. Shenfeld and van Handel supply Ehrhard--Borell convexity and equality cases. Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu are a nonnested architectural comparator: their normal model-based policies optimize expected sample size and familywise error rather than exact complete-cell conditional-randomization local power, so no optimality theorem transfers. Chen and Andrews concern parametric Gaussian adaptive experiments rather than fixed finite populations.
prose_updates.interpretation: The result separates a reusable exact-inference layer from a new design layer. The augmented-action map certifies that the finite reference is a computable specialization of established selective randomization inference at the sharp null. The Gaussian transfer and the ensuing endpoint, interior, and mixed-sign optimizer geometry are additional results, valid uniformly over a common scalar holdout and finitely many active complete-cell coordinates.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The per-array transfer remains qualitative: it controls random complement counts, studentizers, local rank crossings, complete signed-cell conditioning, null imputation, and moving critical values with one \(\eta_n(B)\), but supplies no deterministic rate uniform over all baseline arrays. Finiteness of \(S\) and \(J\) is essential to the joint Cramér--Wold, finite-product cancellation, common margin, and semianalytic refinement arguments. The FZG bridge establishes only representation, computability, and validity; it does not imply the Gaussian approximation or any holdout-power optimum. The two-component mixture remains deliberately two-stratum and certifies interiority, not uniqueness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The strata may form any fixed finite nonempty set, but may not grow with \(n\). The common scalar holdout is chosen from the fixed compact interval \(I\), and only active pairs in finite \(J\) are tested. Finite-sample exactness is confined to the prespecified Fisher sharp-zero null. Positive local alternatives use a shifted sampling law, while each realized dataset creates a separate zero-drift Fisher reference. The FZG relationship is a specialization of their augmented-action representation, not class equivalence; their results do not supply this note's Gaussian transfer or optimizer. Rosenblum--Fang--Liu is nonnested and transfers no optimality claim. The explicit \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\) witness sets \(S=\{1,2\}\) only for that counterexample. General outputs remain set-valued unless an explicit separation certificate proves a unique design.
